state.lastRunNotes: Continued broad macro-driven selloff, not stock-specific: US bond market turmoil (30-year yield highest since 2004, 10-year since 2007) plus an oil price spike from a Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia reviving supply fears are hammering ASX tech/growth names (XRO -35.8%, WTC -30.8%, CAR -25.5%, PLS -25.6%) with no company-specific bad news confirmed for Xero or WiseTech. Volume stays below average across the watchlist (vol_x mostly under 1x), so there's no capitulation/bottom signal worth chasing - this looks like a falling knife, not a catalyst to buy into. Held positions are unchanged: CBA (core) and TLS (core) show no news breaking their horizons, and PME (growth) remains above its A$150 stop. Growth/core balance excluding day-trades is 36.6%/63.4%, inside the 35-65% band, so no rebalance is needed. Holding everything this session.
